subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Should OpenClaw accept replacing the shared inbound system-tag sanitizer with marker/envelope recognition plus system-event queue neutralization as the complete prompt-boundary contract?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes the security model rather than fixing a purely mechanical defect; source-level tests can show selected funnels but cannot choose the repository’s acceptable trust boundary or upgrade posture.

options.title: Accept the narrowed boundary
options.body: Approve the marker, external-envelope, and system-event queue boundaries as the intended contract, retaining the documented Doctor repairs and SDK alias window.

options.title: Preserve broader sanitization
options.body: Keep or replace a shared sanitizer for any prompt-bound external-text path that cannot be exhaustively shown to stay inside a trusted envelope or equivalent boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrowed boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the marker, external-envelope, and system-event queue boundaries as the intended contract, retaining the documented Doctor repairs and SDK alias window.
